title: Rethinking Underwater Image Enhancement: Learning through Text-Guided Degradation Curriculum

problem.summary: Existing paired clean-degraded datasets have advanced learning-based underwater image enhancement, but they remain either limited in scale or difficult to acquire, and still fail to adequately cover the diverse degradations encountered in real-world underwater environments.
statements: Existing paired clean-degraded datasets have advanced learning-based underwater image enhancement, but they remain either limited in scale or difficult to acquire, and still fail to adequately cover the diverse degradations encountered in real-world underwater environments.

Such scarce and insufficient data ultimately restrict the generalization of underwater image enhancement models, highlighting the need for realistic and controllable degradation modeling to better capture real underwater conditions and improve enhancement robustness.
To this end, we propose a unified degradation-aware training framework for the underwater image enhancement task.

solution.summary: Our methodology addresses the challenges of underwater image enhancement through a twostage framework.
solution.approach: Our methodology addresses the challenges of underwater image enhancement through a twostage framework.
components: First, to overcome the bottleneck of limited diversity and fixed degradation patterns in existing datasets, we introduce a TextConditioned Degradation Augmentation (TCDA) pipeline.
This pipeline synthesizes a vast and diverse corpus of degraded images with controllable degradation attributes specified by finegrained text prompts.

Second, leveraging this augmented data, we employ a progressive degradation curriculum to train a Transmission-Guided One-Step Diffusion (TG-Diff) model, designed for transmission-guided image restoration with 4 bank.
